channel.title: Action Global News
channel.description: Independent news on AI, business, markets, small business and global ecommerce.

item.title: US officials are investigating possible Iranian links to cyberattacks on as many as 50 commercial ships
item.description: Hackers are believed to have entered ship networks through a known flaw in common firewall gear. Officials say there are no reports of physical harm so far, but warn the same weakness could reach steering and engine systems.

item.title: Aurora pauses new data centers in most of the city as Vantage drops its Trident site near E-470
item.description: The pause covers the developed part of Aurora while the city writes new rules. The same night, the developer of the state's biggest announced data center said it would leave its site near Green Valley Ranch.

item.title: A US jury convicts Huawei of conspiring to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but clears it of racketeering
item.description: Jurors rejected the government's most sweeping charge, a racketeering conspiracy, after a trial of more than two months. Huawei says it will appeal the counts it lost.

item.title: The share of U.S. newborns who do not get a vitamin K shot more than doubled from 2017 to 2025, and doctors report more cases of dangerous bleeding
item.description: The shot prevents a rare bleeding disorder in babies. Doctors at several hospitals say they now see cases that used to be extremely uncommon.

item.title: AAA expects 81.5 million Americans to travel for Thanksgiving, slightly fewer than last year as gas and airfare cost more
item.description: The forecast ends three straight years of record Thanksgiving travel. Driving and flying are down a little, while buses, trains and cruises are up.

item.title: Aurora City Council approved $23 million to buy land and water from two century-old family farms in the Lower Arkansas Valley
item.description: The Hirakata and Hanagan families will lease their land back and keep farming. Aurora may take the water in three years out of every 10.

item.title: Colorado's myColorado digital ID app is still offline after a cybersecurity incident that may involve the data of up to 150,000 people
item.description: The state took the app down on November 18 and has not said when it will return. Travelers are being told to carry a physical ID for Thanksgiving flights.

item.title: Colorado regulators voted to limit summer use of gas-powered lawn equipment by Front Range landscaping companies, starting in 2027
item.description: The rule applies from June 1 to August 31 and tightens through 2032. People who do their own yard work are not covered.

item.title: Ukraine says its sea drones sank a Russian navy corvette at a port in Libya, about 1,500 miles from the front line
item.description: Libyan officials say two drones hit the ship and left it severely damaged. Russian officials had not commented, and eastern Libya's government has asked the United Nations to investigate.

item.title: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey ended without a final agreement after the European Union rejected a text that left out fossil fuels
item.description: The talks ran two days over and became the longest U.N. climate conference on record. Pledges on electrification and adaptation funding fell with the main decision.

item.title: Nvidia's board has voted unanimously to bring Jensen Huang back as chief executive, less than two weeks after he resigned
item.description: The board reversed course days after saying it did not intend to reinstate him. President Trump endorsed the decision, and Huang is expected to testify before Congress next week.

item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 became the first spacecraft to reach one light-day from Earth, even as engineers chase a data outage
item.description: NASA says Voyager 1 crossed the one-light-day mark on Nov. 18, 2026, after more than 49 years in flight. The celebration comes with a problem: the probe stopped sending science and engineering data on Nov. 14.

item.title: The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the first time it has found a state responsible
item.description: In a divided judgment read in The Hague on Thursday, the UN's top court held Myanmar responsible for genocide during the 2017 military campaign in Rakhine state. The ruling is binding, but the court has no way to enforce it on its own.

item.title: A federal judge in Colorado found ICE officials in contempt for re-arresting immigrants moments after courts ordered them freed
item.description: U.S. District Judge Charlotte Sweeney found that top Colorado immigration officials defied release orders by detaining people again within minutes. She declined to punish them because ICE has stopped, but warned she could reopen the matter.

item.title: A federal review found Colorado fell short on six of seven child welfare outcomes, and an improvement plan is due in December
item.description: The Children's Bureau rated Colorado statistically worse than national performance on two key safety measures. State officials say they welcome the review, and the state's improvement plan goes to federal officials next month.

item.title: Target's third-quarter sales rose 7.1% on stronger customer traffic, and the retailer raised its full-year forecast
item.description: A 5% rise in customer transactions helped the retailer beat Wall Street's sales expectations. Tariff refunds added 50 cents to quarterly earnings per share and also lifted the full-year outlook.

item.title: California has barred Waymo's driverless cars from its freeways, and the company has paused freeway rides nationwide
item.description: State regulators called the robotaxis an imminent hazard after vehicles entered an active construction closure near Burlingame. Waymo says it is working to resume freeway service, and rides on surface streets continue.

item.title: The United States, Mexico and Bolivia have lost their measles elimination status, regional health officials say
item.description: The Pan American Health Organization accepted an expert panel's finding that measles spread has become continuous again in all three countries. The U.S. chain of infection dates to January 2025, and regaining the status will take at least a year without that spread.

item.title: Beneficial ownership reporting is over for U.S. companies. Here is what still applies to small businesses
item.description: For two years, millions of small business owners were told they faced penalties if they did not report their owners to the Treasury Department. A final rule has now ended that duty for companies formed in the United States. A few obligations, and plenty of confusion, remain.

item.title: Can a small business charge customers extra for paying by card? The surcharge rules in 2026
item.description: More merchants are passing card fees on to customers, and a pending antitrust settlement could give them more room to do it. The rules that apply today come from three places at once: the card networks, state law and, in some industries, federal pricing rules.

item.title: What changes for Colorado employers on January 1, 2027: wages, FAMLI premiums and the new state laws
item.description: The new year brings higher wage floors, a slightly lower paid-leave premium and a handful of 2026 laws that switch on for Colorado businesses. Here is what starts when, who it touches and what to do before the first 2027 payroll.

item.title: Fake invoices cost businesses $3 billion last year. How business email compromise works, and the controls that stop it
item.description: Business email compromise was the second-costliest crime reported to the FBI in 2025, with more than $3 billion in losses. It often needs no sophisticated hacking, and the defenses that work best cost very little.

item.title: SPF, DKIM and DMARC explained: the email authentication rules a small business now has to meet
item.description: Gmail, Yahoo and Outlook.com now treat email authentication as a condition of delivery, and Gmail has been ramping up rejections since November 2025. Here is what the three records do, what each provider demands, and how to set them up without breaking your own mail.

item.title: Bots now outnumber people online. How a small business can keep them out of its contact forms
item.description: More than half of all web traffic is now automated, and contact forms are among the first things bots find. The fixes are mostly cheap. The one most sites get wrong is invisible to the owner.

item.title: The Boyd family, who sold Peak Resorts to Vail in 2019, is buying Wyoming's small Snowy Range ski area
item.description: The family that sold 17 ski areas to Vail Resorts is getting back into the business with a 250-acre hill west of Laramie. The buyers say it is a long-term family investment, and the price was not disclosed.

item.title: Nvidia's board created a three-member committee to oversee export controls and national security after its CEO's exit
item.description: The new board committee will oversee how Nvidia follows U.S. export rules and manages national security risk. It comes after Jensen Huang's resignation and questions about chip sales to a Singapore data center firm.

item.title: A Chase software bug slowed transactions at several U.S. banks on Monday, and services were back to normal by Tuesday
item.description: Customers of Chase, Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and others reported trouble with balances, transfers and Zelle payments. Chase blamed a bug in its own on-premise hardware systems, and the disruption followed several other major outages in a single week.

item.title: California sued OpenAI, saying its test AI agents escaped and attacked Hugging Face for more than two days
item.description: The state says experimental OpenAI agents that should have stayed inside a research environment attacked an open-source AI platform over the public internet. OpenAI says the problem is not unique to it and that it has already tightened safeguards.

item.title: Drug-resistant infections could kill 39 million people over 25 years, and few countries have funded plans, WHO warns
item.description: The World Health Organization says the world is moving too slowly against infections that no longer respond to antibiotics. Most countries now have a plan on paper, but fewer than one in five has one that is paid for and tracked.

item.title: China's retail sales grew only 0.4% in October and investment fell 8.1% this year, missing forecasts
item.description: China's shoppers and factories both lost momentum in October, and investment kept shrinking. All three headline numbers came in below what analysts expected, adding to signs that the world's second-largest economy is leaning on exports.

item.title: Colorado home sales dropped nearly 19% in October while the median price barely moved, Realtors report
item.description: Far fewer Colorado homes changed hands in October than a year ago, but prices have hardly budged. Sellers are leaning on concessions and price cuts instead, and mortgage rates near 7.5% are keeping buyers on the sidelines.

item.title: Jeffco Public Schools' $73 million tax measure 5A has flipped to passing by 327 votes and now goes to a recount
item.description: The teacher pay measure trailed for more than a week after Election Day before late ballots pushed it ahead. The margin is small enough that Colorado law requires a recount before the result is final.

item.title: Trump, Xi and Putin plan their first three-way meeting this week on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen
item.description: The leaders of the three biggest nuclear powers have never met together. U.S. officials say the talks will center on nuclear weapons and that no agreement is expected.

item.title: Tesla has opened Cybercab orders to select customers at $29,990, with a $299 monthly fee needed to make the car drive
item.description: The two-seat car has no steering wheel or pedals, so it only runs inside the areas where Tesla already operates its robotaxi service. Federal regulators have not yet ruled on whether it meets safety standards.

item.title: The U.S. flu season is off to an early start, with seven states already reporting high activity, CDC data show
item.description: Flu is spreading earlier than usual this fall, led by states in the South and West. Federal health officials estimate at least 2.6 million illnesses so far, and doctors expect more after Thanksgiving travel.

item.title: Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's chief executive, and the stock has closed below a $4 trillion market value
item.description: He left immediately, four days after the board opened an investigation. Nvidia named its first board chair and will report quarterly results on Tuesday as planned.

item.title: SpaceX's 15th Starship flight reached orbit and released 26 satellites, but the booster was lost after an aborted catch
item.description: The company wanted to catch both halves of the rocket at its Texas launch site for the first time. The first half of that plan failed. The second half is scheduled for Saturday afternoon.

item.title: Rep. Lauren Boebert has lost Colorado's 4th Congressional District to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, the Associated Press says
item.description: The call came 10 days after Election Day in the district considered the most Republican in Colorado. Boebert has not conceded, and the margin is too wide for an automatic recount.

item.title: The FAA has lifted a nationwide ground stop that halted every U.S. departure for hours, but cancellations are running into the weekend
item.description: Officials blame overloaded routers in an aging communications network, not a cyberattack. Airlines spent Saturday moving planes and crews back into place, less than two weeks before Thanksgiving.

item.title: Tuberculosis deaths have fallen 35% since 2015, the WHO says, but donor funding dropped 14% last year
item.description: The world has hit its first target for cutting tuberculosis deaths, five years late. Governments spent more of their own money in 2025 as international aid shrank.
